title: Hydrating messages does not rebuild turn-to-conversation routing
reasoning: The store keeps a global turnConversationRefs index used to resolve later turn-scoped events to a conversation. addMessage and updateMessage maintain that index, but setMessages replaces a workspace's full message list without indexing any message turnRefs. Any caller that hydrates or restores a conversation with setMessages will display the messages but leave resolveConversationRefForTurn unable to resolve their turns, so subsequent turn-scoped updates can fail to find the intended workspace.
reproduction: Call setMessages([{ id: 'm1', text: 'x', sender: 'assistant', turnRef: 'turn-1' }], 'conv-a'), then resolveConversationRefForTurn('turn-1'); it returns null because setMessages only updates the workspace messages array.
recommendation: When setMessages receives a concrete normalized conversationRef, derive normalized turn refs from the provided messages and merge them into turnConversationRefs. If setMessages is intentionally display-only, split that API from a hydration API and document the difference with tests.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were linked for this feature, so the index-maintenance contract is not exercised across addMessage, updateMessage, and setMessages.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a store test that calls setMessages with messages containing turnRef for a non-active conversation and verifies resolveConversationRefForTurn maps those turns to that conversation.
minimumFixScope: Extend setMessages to update turnConversationRefs for message.turnRef values when the target conversation can be normalized.
